name: PawStyle by Lola — Dual Agent Dispatch (steering variant)
description: Two parallel agents build Lola's boutique dog apparel store. Backend gets a steering event at turn 3 for Lola-tested breed-specific sizing. Inspired by @_justlolathings.

turns.content:
Build a product listing page for PawStyle by Lola — a boutique dog apparel store inspired by Lola (@_justlolathings), the most fashionable pup on Instagram.

Requirements:
- HTML page with embedded CSS and JS
- Header: "PawStyle by Lola" with tagline "Where every pup is a fashionista"
- Purple gradient header (#7c3aed to #6d28d9)
- 6 products in a flexbox grid (3 columns, responsive) on lavender (#e9d5ff) cards:
  1. Lola's Signature Bandana - $12.00 (show "Lola's Pick" badge)
  2. Cozy Knit Sweater - $35.00
  3. Rainy Day Raincoat - $45.00
  4. Adventure Booties (4-pack) - $28.00
  5. Dapper Bow Tie - $15.00 (show "Lola's Pick" badge)
  6. Walk-in-Style Harness - $40.00
- Each card: product name, price, placeholder image (300x200 gray), card shadow (0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.1))
- Size selector dropdown per card: XS (Chihuahua), S (Pom), M (Beagle), L (Lab), XL (Golden)
- 'Add to Cart' button per card (purple #7c3aed background, white text)
- Footer with link to Lola's Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/_justlolathings/
- Fetch products from GET http://localhost:8080/api/products on page load
- Fallback to hardcoded data if API unavailable

Write all files needed. Use the write_file tool for each file.

Files written. Lola's shop looks fantastic! Now add a Cart sidebar that slides in from the right when any 'Add to Cart' is clicked. It should show item name, selected size (with breed label), price, and a total. Use the write_file tool to update the file.

Cart sidebar done. Backend team just added a Lola-tested size guide endpoint! Add a 'Size Guide' button next to each size selector that opens a modal. The modal fetches GET http://localhost:8080/api/size-guide/generic and displays Lola's breed-specific sizing table with columns for size, breed example, chest, neck, and weight. Title the modal 'Lola-Tested Sizing for Every Breed'. Use write_file to update.

Build the REST API for PawStyle by Lola — a boutique dog apparel store — using Python stdlib (http.server, no frameworks).

Endpoints:
- GET /api/products — returns JSON array of all 6 products:
  [{"id": 1, "name": "Lola's Signature Bandana", "price": 12.00, "sizes": ["XS","S","M","L","XL"], "image": "/img/bandana.jpg", "lola_pick": true},
   {"id": 2, "name": "Cozy Knit Sweater", "price": 35.00, "sizes": ["XS","S","M","L","XL"], "image": "/img/sweater.jpg", "lola_pick": false},
   {"id": 3, "name": "Rainy Day Raincoat", "price": 45.00, "sizes": ["XS","S","M","L","XL"], "image": "/img/raincoat.jpg", "lola_pick": false},
   {"id": 4, "name": "Adventure Booties (4-pack)", "price": 28.00, "sizes": ["XS","S","M","L","XL"], "image": "/img/booties.jpg", "lola_pick": false},
   {"id": 5, "name": "Dapper Bow Tie", "price": 15.00, "sizes": ["XS","S","M","L","XL"], "image": "/img/bowtie.jpg", "lola_pick": true},
   {"id": 6, "name": "Walk-in-Style Harness", "price": 40.00, "sizes": ["XS","S","M","L","XL"], "image": "/img/harness.jpg", "lola_pick": false}]
- GET /api/products/<id> — returns single product or 404
- CORS headers on all responses (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *)
- Listen on port 8080

Use write_file tool for each file.

Server file written. Add input validation — product IDs must be 1-6, return proper 400 for invalid IDs (not just 404). Add a health endpoint GET /api/health that returns {"status": "ok", "store": "PawStyle by Lola", "products_count": 6}. Use write_file.

STEERING EVENT: Frontend team just added a Size Guide button to each product card. You need to add Lola's breed-specific sizing endpoint:

GET /api/size-guide/:breed

Return JSON with Lola-tested sizing for every breed:
{"breed": "<breed>", "tagline": "Lola-tested sizing for every breed", "sizes": {"XS": {"breed_example": "Chihuahua", "chest": "10-13in", "neck": "8-10in", "weight": "2-6lbs"}, "S": {"breed_example": "Pomeranian", "chest": "13-16in", "neck": "10-12in", "weight": "6-12lbs"}, "M": {"breed_example": "Beagle", "chest": "16-22in", "neck": "12-16in", "weight": "12-35lbs"}, "L": {"breed_example": "Labrador", "chest": "22-28in", "neck": "16-20in", "weight": "35-70lbs"}, "XL": {"breed_example": "Golden Retriever", "chest": "28-34in", "neck": "20-24in", "weight": "70-100lbs"}}}

For breed='generic', return the default table above. For specific breeds (labrador, pomeranian, beagle, chihuahua, golden), adjust the measurements to be breed-specific. Unknown breeds return the generic table.

This is urgent — frontend is waiting on Lola's sizing guide. Use write_file to update server.py.
